subject: Finexus — urgent: spike in 95p latency and error rate after v3.2.1 + QP-5
messages:
From: Michael Yang <michael.yang@finexus.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@finexus.com
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Production impact after v3.2.1 + QP-5 deploy (p95/ERR spike)

Hi Rishi,

We pushed live this morning around 02:45 UTC the model upgrade you shipped (v3.2.1 + quant profile QP-5). Since ~07:45 PDT we've seen a ~2.5x increase in 95th latency for our inference route and a steady increase in server errors (5xx) on ~3% of requests. There is also a measurable drop in answer quality on our regression prompt set (examples attached).

Attached: finexus_perf.pdf (summary graphs), sample_responses.txt (quality diffs).

This is impacting checkout flows for a subset of our customers. We need either an immediate rollback to the previous model or a hotfix within the next 2 hours. Please advise the plan and timeline — we are on standby and can provide logs/trace IDs.

-Michael
CTO, Finexus

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Michael Yang <michael.yang@finexus.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production impact after v3.2.1 + QP-5 deploy (p95/ERR spike)

Thanks Michael — I see the graphs. Sorry for the disruption. We're treating this as P1.

Quick questions while we triage:
- Can you confirm the percentage of traffic routed to Redwood vs cached responses?
- Any specific user segments affected (region / plan)?

I'm looping in Marissa (Customer Success), Aditya (Engineering), and Lauren (Product) to coordinate rollback and triage. We'll propose a rollback or targeted routing change in the next 20–30 minutes.

I'll keep you posted on the timeline.

—Rishi
VP, Sales (Redwood Inference)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Action: Finexus v3.2.1 rollback plan / immediate tasks

Team — Finexus (DN-4382) reports p95/5xx spike after v3.2.1 + QP-5. Customer impact: checkout retries and degraded answers. Exec (CTO) wants rollback ASAP. Please action below: 

- Marissa: Confirm rollback comms and SLA acceptability with customer; propose 45-minute ETA for the first rollback window. Use the message in the draft doc in Drive. (att: rollback_playbook.md)
- Aditya: Prepare rollback to v3.1.8 and a quick quant mapping patch (qp_mapping.diff). Confirm whether stateful cache invalidation is required.
- Lauren: Verify release config and routing for Finexus's tenant (region: us-west). Check autoscaler thresholds that might have contributed to 5xx.
- Evelyn: Please join the executive update in 30 min and prep an incident summary for the leadership thread.

Notes / constraints:
- We suspect the new QP-5 uses a denser int8 mapping that increases kernel load on p99 paths; the runtime's kernel selector may be switching to slower fallback kernels for certain sequence-length distributions.
- Rolling back model binary is lower-risk than attempting an on-the-fly re-quantization.

I've created SUP-3129 and uploaded the initial artifacts: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-3129
Attachments: rollback_playbook.md

I'll own communications to Michael until Marissa takes over.

—Rishi

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Action: Finexus v3.2.1 rollback plan / immediate tasks

Short update from runtime/infra perspective:

- Reproduced p95 spike locally using Finexus trace set (thanks for the samples). The problematic path appears when tokens > 384 and batching pushes some minibatches into a fallback attention kernel that is noticeably slower under QP-5.
- Rolling back to v3.1.8 (previous quant profile QP-4) should restore prior latency characteristics. Rolling back is a ~20–35 minute operation for Finexus tenant (including cache warm-up).
- Alternative: apply qp_mapping.diff which remaps a small subset of layers to the QP-4 quant table. That avoids full model swap but is riskier for quality. Risk: we may see small regressions in corner cases; requires immediate smoke tests.

I will stage the rollback bundle now. I'll also prepare the qp_mapping.diff as a hotfix in case the customer prefers a smaller change.

Attachments: qp_mapping.diff
—Aditya
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Michael Yang <michael.yang@finexus.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Production impact after v3.2.1 + QP-5 deploy (p95/ERR spike)

Michael — update and plan: 

- Root cause hypothesis: under Finexus request patterns (more long prompts per session) the QP-5 quant profile causes the runtime to pick a slower fallback kernel, increasing p95 and a small window of 5xx as backpressure builds.
- Planned action: Rollback to v3.1.8 for your tenant starting at 09:45 PDT. Estimated full recovery by 10:15 PDT (includes cache warm-up).
- Contingency: If you prefer incremental change we can apply a targeted qp mapping hotfix (15–20 minute deploy) after smoke tests.

We will run smoke tests on your regression prompt set immediately and confirm before switching traffic. Link to incident artifacts: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/runbooks/finexus-incident-20270607

Please confirm that 09:45 PDT (09:45) works for Finexus and whether you want a full rollback or the hotfix route.

—Rishi

From: Michael Yang <michael.yang@finexus.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@finexus.com
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production impact after v3.2.1 + QP-5 deploy (p95/ERR spike)

Thanks Rishi — 09:45 PDT rollback is fine. Please proceed with the full rollback to v3.1.8. We want stability over experimental fixes; we can revisit quant profile improvements in a test environment first. Please include a postmortem and recommended mitigations (canary length, perf gate for quant profiles).

-Michael
CTO, Finexus
